title.en: Soil erosion and conservation of fossil fuels

text.en: Soil takes centuries to form but only a few storms to be lost. Coal and petroleum take millions of years to form but we use them in decades.

Soil erosion is removal of the fertile top soil, rich in humus and minerals, by wind and water.
Agents of erosion: high speed wind, flowing water, landslides, deforestation, farming, mining and overgrazing.
Control: keep vegetation cover, control grazing, crop rotation, store runoff, terracing, contour ploughing, shelter belts of trees.
Non-renewable energy (coal, petroleum, natural gas, nuclear) supplies about 90 percent of commercial energy and cannot be renewed quickly.
Fossil fuels formed from buried dead organisms over millions of years by heat and pressure into hydrocarbons.
Coal produces electricity in thermal power plants; petroleum gives petrol, diesel, kerosene and LPG.
Conserve fuels by saving electricity, cycling short distances, using pressure cookers and fuel efficient engines.
Case study: the Mathura refinery releases sulphur and nitrogen oxides that yellowed the Taj Mahal marble, so emission standards were set.

problem.en: Suggest three ways a farmer on a slope can prevent soil erosion.

text.en: Terracing makes level steps that slow runoff.
Contour ploughing runs furrows across the slope.
Planting trees as shelter belts reduces wind erosion.

prompt.en: Why should coal and petroleum be conserved though they are made of biomass?

requiredIdeas.en: They take millions of years to form
Use is far faster than formation

points.en: Prevent by vegetation, terracing, contour ploughing.
